History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
35-year-old man with no significant past medical history presents via telehealth with a 4-day history of sore throat, clear rhinorrhoea/congestion, new dry cough, night sweats, low-grade fever initially, fatigue, myalgias, and mild exertional breathlessness—overall picture most consistent with an acute viral upper respiratory tract infection; supportive care advised.

History:
• Presenting complaint: “Under the weather” ×4 days.  
• Timeline  
  – Day 0: Exposed to co-worker with URI symptoms. Developed painful sore throat; odynophagia for 1-2 days; low-grade fever.  
  – Day 1–3: Runny nose with clear discharge progressing to nasal congestion; sore throat improving. Night sweats began. Intermittent generalized headaches. Started OTC paracetamol and ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) with good fever control.  
  – Day 3–4 (yesterday): New persistent dry cough; still congested; muscle aches started. Mild shortness of breath only on exertion; no dyspnoea at rest.  
• Associated symptoms: Fatigue, decreased appetite, increased fluid intake.  
• Pertinent negatives: No chest pain, wheeze, nausea, vomiting, photophobia, visual changes, ear pain/discharge, rashes, bowel or urinary changes.  
• Review of systems (additional): No joint swelling, no weight loss (not discussed), mood good.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic illnesses reported; “otherwise fit and well.”  
• Medications: Paracetamol and ibuprofen PRN (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives alone.  
• Occupation: Accountant; current workload high but tolerable.  
• Tobacco: Occasional cigars at company events (non-daily).  
• Alcohol: Occasional social use; not a heavy drinker.  
• Recreational drugs: None mentioned.

Family History:
• Maternal grandmother – Type 2 diabetes.  
• Great-grandfather – Eczema.  
• No known family HTN, CAD, malignancy otherwise.

Physical Examination:
(Telehealth visit – no in-person exam.)  
• Vitals: Not obtained.  
• General appearance: Not formally documented via video; patient able to converse in full sentences without apparent distress.

Investigations:
• None ordered or reported.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection (probable common cold; influenza or mild COVID-19 also possible).  
  – Counselled that typical course is 7–10 days; currently day 4 with improving sore throat.  
  – Continue symptomatic treatment: paracetamol and/or ibuprofen as needed, adequate rest, maintain hydration.  
  – Advised taking 1–2 days off work.  
  – Warning signs reviewed: high or persistent fever, worsening breathlessness, chest pain, or failure to improve by next week → seek earlier review.

Issue 2: Exertional dyspnoea associated with URI congestion/cough.  
  – Monitor; should resolve as infection clears.  
  – If breathlessness increases at rest, instructed to seek urgent assessment.

Issue 3: Night sweats.  
  – Likely constitutional symptom of current viral illness; monitor course.  
  – If persisting beyond resolution of URI or accompanied by weight loss/lymphadenopathy, will require further evaluation.

Follow-up:  
• Routine follow-up in 1 week if symptoms not improving or sooner if red-flag symptoms develop.  
• Patient advised how to access care and re-contact clinician.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Viral upper respiratory tract infection (common cold) – High likelihood. Classic sequential symptom pattern (sore throat → rhinorrhoea/congestion → dry cough) with self-limited course already improving.  
2. Influenza – Moderate likelihood. Fever, myalgias, headache and cough fit; however, fever brief and overall symptoms milder than typical flu.  
3. Mild COVID-19 – Moderate likelihood. Overlapping URI symptoms, night sweats and exertional dyspnoea; absence of anosmia and quick improvement make it less typical but still possible given current epidemiology.

Quality checks:
● Missing/expected elements: No documented vitals, physical exam findings, medication doses, vaccination status, COVID testing status.  
● Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor conversational fillers but clinically adequate.
